questions: Could you introduce yourself and describe your background?
What specific area of AI are you most drawn to?
What specific project(s) have you worked on that demonstrate your skills in machine learning or natural language processing?
What does “embedding” represent in the context of machine learning?
Can you explain how you would approach debugging an issue when you’re encountering errors in your machine learning code?
answers: I am a Computer Science student currently in my final year. During my studies, I learned programming fundamentals, databases, software development concepts, and some basic machine learning concepts. I became interested in AI because I think it has many practical applications and I wanted to understand how these systems work.

I am most interested in the area of machine learning and natural language processing because I find it interesting how AI systems can understand and process information.

I am particularly curious about applications like chatbots, recommendation systems, and tools that can help people automate tasks. I have experimented with some basic machine learning models and AI APIs, and I would like to deepen my knowledge of how these systems are built and improved.

I am still exploring different areas of AI, but I am especially interested in understanding how models learn from data and how they can be integrated into practical applications.

During my studies, I worked on a few projects that helped me get familiar with machine learning concepts. One example was a machine learning project where I used a dataset to train a classification model and evaluate its performance using common metrics.

I also worked on a small natural language processing project where I experimented with text classification. I used existing libraries to preprocess text data, convert it into numerical representations, and train a model to classify different categories of text.

These projects helped me understand the basic workflow of an AI project, including preparing data, training models, testing results, and analyzing performance. However, most of my experience is from academic projects, and I am still looking to gain more experience with larger real-world AI applications.

An embedding is a numerical representation of data, such as text, images, or other types of information, that allows machine learning models to understand relationships between different inputs.

For example, in natural language processing, words or sentences can be converted into vectors of numbers. Similar words or sentences will have similar embeddings, which helps models identify patterns and similarities.

Embeddings are commonly used in applications like search engines, recommendation systems, and natural language processing tasks. I understand the general concept, but I have mostly worked with embeddings at a basic level rather than implementing advanced embedding models myself.

When I encounter errors in machine learning code, I usually start by looking at the error message and trying to understand where the problem is happening. I check the relevant part of the code, add some print statements or logs, and verify that the inputs and outputs have the expected format.

For machine learning projects, I would also check the dataset and preprocessing steps because problems can often come from incorrect data, missing values, or unexpected formats.

If the issue is related to the model performance rather than an error, I would analyze metrics, check the training process, and compare the results with expected behavior. I also use documentation and online resources when I encounter unfamiliar errors.

For example, I once had a classification model that was not performing well. I investigated the data preprocessing pipeline and found that the data was not properly normalized, which affected the model's performance. After fixing the preprocessing step, the results improved.
